reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: AI in education and future skills
themes.definition: AI appears in the context of schooling and skills: AI in lessons, teaching AI skills, and preparing young people to use, question and govern AI.
themes.inclusion: Include passages about AI in classrooms, AI-related curricula or skills, or equipping youth to lead technological transformation.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general education passages that mention only digital literacy without AI.
themes.boundary_cases: The rhetorical contrast of children using AI versus lacking schools is also an AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE illustration.

examples.quote: we are considering the teaching, understanding, and use of AI and AI related skills to enhance education access, delivery, and outcome
We must prepare young people not only to use new technologies, but to question them, govern them, and deploy them ethically.

themes.label: Unequal access to AI between countries
themes.definition: AI is used to illustrate or warn against a divide between those who can access and afford innovation and those who cannot.
themes.inclusion: Include passages contrasting AI-enabled and deprived populations or insisting that AI access be equitable.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages about AI benefits that do not raise access inequality.
themes.boundary_cases: Rhetorical paradox framings (children using AI vs walking miles for water) count here even without policy demands.

examples.quote: In another, children are using artificial intelligence in their lessons. a further paradox.
must not create another divide between those countries that can afford to innovate and those that cannot

themes.label: Governance frameworks balancing innovation and protection
themes.definition: Call for credible AI governance frameworks that encourage innovation while protecting privacy, security, democratic values and public trust.
themes.inclusion: Include calls for AI governance frameworks, whether national or international, balancing innovation and protection.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages only about AI education.
themes.boundary_cases: Protection of privacy and democratic values may also be coded AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS.

examples.quote: we must develop credible AI governance frameworks that encourage innovation while protecting people, privacy, security, democratic values, and public trust

themes.label: AI possibilities for sectors of development
themes.definition: AI is framed as offering possibilities for education, health, agriculture, public administration and economic development.
themes.inclusion: Include listings of development sectors that AI can benefit.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages focused solely on risk.
themes.boundary_cases: If paired immediately with an equity caveat, also code AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: offer enormous possibilities for education, healthcare, agriculture, public administration, and economic development

value.rationale: Grenada's passages centre AI within an education agenda, from the rhetorical paradox of AI-using classrooms versus deprived children to teaching AI skills; 2026 adds development opportunities, equitable access and governance frameworks.
